The Philips S396 is a discontinued dual-SIM smartphone released in June 2015. The Prestigio MultiPhone 7600 Duo is a discontinued Dual SIM Android 4.2 smartphone released in early 2014. The Cubot Tab KingKong is a rugged Android 13 tablet released in August 2023, featuring IP68/IP69K dust and water resistance. Released in September 2023, the Honor V Purse is a 5G foldable smartphone featuring a 7.71-inch 90Hz OLED main display and a 6.45-inch cover display, both with 1600 nits peak brightness. The O2 XDA Comet is a discontinued smartphone released in September 2007, running Windows Mobile 6.0 Professional on an Intel XScale 620 MHz CPU. Released in October 2023, the Oppo A79 is a 5G-enabled smartphone featuring a 6.72-inch 90Hz IPS LCD display and a Mediatek Dimensity 6020 chipset. It is equipped with 8GB RAM, 128GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a 50MP dual main camera system. The device is powered by a 5000 mAh battery with 33W fast charging and includes stereo speakers and IPX4 splash resistance.

The ZTE Blade A73 5G is an affordable Android 13 smartphone released in September 2023. It features a 6.52-inch 90Hz IPS LCD display, a Unisoc T760 chipset, 4GB of RAM, and 128GB of internal storage. Key highlights include 5G connectivity, a 50MP dual main camera, and a large 5000 mAh battery, priced at approximately €129.

The Sagem Puma Phone is a discontinued 2010 device tailored for fitness, featuring a built-in solar cell, pedometer, and bike/run trackers. It has a 2.8-inch resistive touchscreen, a 3.15 MP main camera, and basic HSPA connectivity. It is powered by a removable 880 mAh battery and was originally priced around 400 EUR.

Released in November 2019, the Cat S52 is a rugged smartphone featuring MIL-STD-810G compliance, IP68 water/dust resistance, and drop-to-concrete protection. It is equipped with a 5.65-inch IPS LCD (720x1440), a Mediatek Helio P35 octa-core processor, 4GB RAM, and 64GB of storage. The device includes a 12MP main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and a 3100 mAh battery, priced at approximately 440 EUR.

The Oppo Reno11 (China), released in late 2023, is a 5G-enabled smartphone featuring a 6.7-inch 120Hz OLED display with peak brightness of 950 nits. It is powered by the Mediatek Dimensity 8200 chipset, Android 14, and offers storage options up to 512GB with up to 12GB RAM. The device boasts a triple main camera setup led by a 50MP wide sensor with OIS, a 32MP telephoto lens, and a 32MP selfie camera. It is equipped with a 4800 mAh battery supporting 67W fast charging and is priced at approximately 320 EUR.

Released in November 2018, the Panasonic P85 Nxt is an entry-level Android 7.1.2 smartphone featuring a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display (720p) and a Snapdragon 210 quad-core processor. It is equipped with 2GB RAM, 16GB internal storage, an 8MP main camera, and a 5MP selfie camera. A notable highlight is its large 4000 mAh battery, and it includes a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor, priced at approximately 7000 INR.

The BenQ-Siemens EF61 is a discontinued GSM phone launched in July 2006. It is a compact device weighing 99g, featuring a primary TFT display (128x160 pixels) and a secondary external CSTN screen. Key specs include a 1.3 MP main camera, 1.5MB internal memory with a microSD slot, Bluetooth, and a removable 750 mAh battery providing up to 3 hours of talk time.

The Alcatel 1B (2022) is an entry-level smartphone released in May 2022, priced around 100 EUR. It features a 5.5-inch TFT LCD display (720x1440), is powered by a Mediatek Helio A22 chipset with 2GB RAM and 32GB storage, and runs Android 11 (Go edition). It includes an 8MP main camera, a 5MP selfie camera, and a removable 3000 mAh battery.

The T-Mobile Revvlry, released in July 2019, is a budget-friendly Android 9.0 smartphone priced around 180 EUR. It features a 5.7-inch IPS LCD display (720x1520), a Snapdragon 632 octa-core processor, 3GB of RAM, and 32GB of internal storage. Key hardware includes a 13MP main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and a 3000 mAh battery with 10W wired charging. Released in November 2023, the Honor X50i+ is a slim (6.8mm) 5G smartphone featuring a 6.7-inch 90Hz AMOLED display with a peak brightness of 2000 nits. It is powered by a Dimensity 6080 chipset, 12GB of RAM, and storage options of 256GB or 512GB. Key highlights include a 108MP main camera, a 4500mAh battery with 35W wired charging, and Android 13, priced at approximately 210 EUR.

Released in May 2019, the Vodafone Smart N10 is an entry-level Android 9.0 smartphone priced at approximately 150 EUR. It features a 5.67-inch IPS LCD display, a Mediatek Helio A22 quad-core processor, 2GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage. The device is equipped with a 13MP main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and a 2920 mAh battery.

Released in December 2021, the Philips PH1 is an affordable Android smartphone (approx. 70 EUR) featuring a 6.51-inch IPS LCD display and a 4700 mAh battery. It is powered by a Unisoc Tiger T310 chipset with 4GB of RAM and storage options ranging from 32GB to 128GB. The device includes a 13MP dual main camera, a 5MP selfie camera, and supports LTE connectivity via Dual SIM.

The Sony Ericsson Xperia active is a discontinued, rugged compact smartphone released in October 2011. It features a 3.0-inch LED-backlit LCD, IP67 dust and water resistance, and a built-in flashlight. The Sharp Aquos V6, released in February 2022, is an entry-level Android 12 smartphone priced around 130 EUR. It features a 6.52-inch IPS LCD display (720 x 1600), a Mediatek Helio G25 chipset with 3GB RAM and 32GB storage, and a large 5000 mAh battery with USB Power Delivery 3.0. The OnePlus Nord CE 3 Lite, released in April 2023, is a budget-friendly 5G smartphone featuring a large 6.72-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display and a Snapdragon 695 5G chipset. It is highlighted by a high-resolution 108MP main camera, 8GB of RAM with up to 256GB of storage, and a 5000 mAh battery supporting fast 67W wired charging. The device runs Android 13 and includes stereo speakers and a 3.5mm headphone jack.

Released in May 2019, the Archos Oxygen 63 is an entry-level Android 9.0 smartphone priced around 130 EUR. It features a 6.26-inch IPS LCD display (720x1520), a Unisoc SC9863 octa-core chipset, 4GB of RAM, and 64GB of internal storage. The device is equipped with a dual rear camera (8MP main), a 5MP selfie camera, and a removable 3000 mAh battery.

The Parla Mist is a discontinued 2G feature phone released in late 2012. It features a compact design with a QWERTY keyboard, a small 1.8-inch TFT display, and a unique Triple SIM capability. Notable features include an under-display fingerprint sensor, a motorized pop-up 8MP selfie camera, and a dual 16MP main camera. It is equipped with a 3450 mAh battery supporting 18W wired and wireless charging, priced at approximately 360 EUR.

The i-mobile Hitz 2206 is a discontinued 2010 dual-SIM GSM feature phone featuring a QWERTY keyboard, a 220x176 pixel TFT display, and a basic 0.3MP main camera. It lacks modern connectivity like WLAN, Bluetooth, and USB, but includes a stereo FM radio and a removable 1000 mAh battery providing up to 4 hours of talk time.

The Eten glofiish X900, released in June 2008, is a discontinued Windows Mobile 6.1 Professional smartphone. The Sony Ericsson Xperia mini pro is a discontinued compact smartphone released in August 2011. The Posh Volt Max LTE L640 is a discontinued Android 5.1 smartphone released in June 2016. It is characterized by a large 6.44-inch IPS LCD display and a massive 6000 mAh battery. Hardware specs include a Mediatek MT6753 octa-core processor, 3GB of RAM, and storage options of 32GB or 64GB. It features a 13MP main camera and an 8MP selfie camera, with connectivity supporting 4G LTE, Dual SIM, and microUSB.

The VK Mobile VK4000 is a discontinued GSM feature phone announced in March 2006. It is a compact, lightweight device (79g) featuring a 1.8-inch TFT display, a VGA main camera, and 128MB of internal memory. Key features include Bluetooth connectivity, Java support, and an MP3/AAC player, powered by a removable 800mAh Li-Ion battery. It was originally priced at approximately 60 EUR.

The itel A70 is an entry-level Android 13 (Go edition) smartphone released in November 2023. The Sendo X is a discontinued GSM mobile phone released in Q4 2003. Connectivity is limited to Bluetooth 1.1, an infrared port, and a proprietary USB port, powered by a removable 1050 mAh battery.

The Realme Narzo 60x is a budget-friendly 5G smartphone released in September 2023, priced at ₹12,999. It features a 6.72-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display, a Dimensity 6100+ chipset, and comes with options for 4GB or 6GB of RAM and 128GB of internal storage. Key hardware includes a 50MP dual rear camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and a large 5000mAh battery supporting 33W fast charging.

The LG K92 5G, released in November 2020, is a 5G-enabled smartphone featuring a large 6.7-inch IPS LCD display (1080 x 2400) and a Snapdragon 690 5G chipset. It is equipped with 128GB storage, 6GB RAM, and a 4000mAh battery with Quick Charge 4.0. Notable hardware includes a 64MP quad-camera system capable of 4K video, a 16MP selfie camera, stereo speakers, and a side-mounted fingerprint sensor.

The device includes a 50MP dual main camera system with OIS, a 32MP selfie camera, and a 4400mAh battery supporting 68W wired and 15W wireless charging.

The Innostream INNO 36 was a compact GSM phone announced in Q2 2005 but ultimately cancelled. It was powered by a removable 920mAh Li-Ion battery.

Notable for its symmetrical camera setup, it has 13MP sensors for both the main and selfie cameras. It is powered by a non-removable 3000 mAh battery and supports Dual SIM LTE connectivity.

The Dell Streak 7 Wi-Fi is a discontinued Android tablet released in April 2011. The AT&T Quickfire is a discontinued QWERTY keyboard phone released in November 2008. It features a 2.8-inch TFT display (240x320 pixels), a 1.3 MP main camera, and basic HSPA network connectivity. The Fairphone 4 is a durable, 5G-enabled smartphone released in October 2021, featuring a 6.3-inch IPS LCD display and a Snapdragon 750G chipset. Notably, it is built for longevity and ruggedness, boasting MIL-STD-810G compliance, a removable 3905 mAh battery, and a standard 5-year warranty.

Key features include a dual rear camera (8MP + 2MP), a 5MP selfie camera, a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor, and a removable 2000 mAh battery.

The Maxwest Gravity 5 LTE is a discontinued entry-level smartphone released in February 2016. It features a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display (480x854), a dual-core 1.3 GHz CPU, and minimal memory with 512MB RAM and 4GB internal storage. It is equipped with an 8MP main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and a 2000 mAh battery.

The Sony Ericsson Xperia Arc S is a discontinued Android smartphone released in September 2011. It features a 4.2-inch LED-backlit LCD display, a 1.4 GHz Snapdragon S2 processor, and 512MB of RAM. Notable hardware includes an 8MP main camera capable of 720p video, a removable 1500 mAh battery, and an HDMI port. It originally launched with Android 2.3.4, upgradable to 4.0.4.

Released in November 2023, the Honor 100 is a 5G-enabled smartphone featuring a 6.7-inch 120Hz OLED display with a peak brightness of 2600 nits. It is powered by the Qualcomm Snapdragon 7 Gen 3 chipset, offering up to 16GB of RAM and 512GB of internal storage. The device boasts a 50MP main camera with OIS and a 50MP selfie camera, both supporting 4K video. It is equipped with a 5000mAh battery supporting fast 100W wired charging, and is priced at approximately 320 EUR.

Released in July 2023, the Tecno Pova 5 is an Android 13 smartphone featuring a large 6.78-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display and a Mediatek Helio G99 chipset. It offers 8GB of RAM with storage options of 128GB or 256GB, a 50MP main camera, and a massive 6000mAh battery with 45W fast charging. Priced at approximately ₹11,999, it includes stereo speakers, NFC, and a side-mounted fingerprint sensor.

The Sagem my721z is a discontinued GSM feature phone released in February 2008. It features a 2.2-inch TFT display, a 3.15 MP main camera, and a removable 1000mAh Li-Ion battery providing up to 3 hours of talk time. Key connectivity includes Bluetooth, GPRS, and an FM radio, while memory is expandable via a dedicated microSD slot.

Released in June 2023, the BLU G73 is an affordable Android 13 smartphone priced around 140 EUR. It features a large 6.8-inch 90Hz IPS LCD display, an octa-core CPU, 6GB of RAM, and 128GB of internal storage. Key hardware includes a 50MP triple main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and a long-lasting 5000mAh battery with 18W wired charging. The device is built with an eco-leather back and includes a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor.

Released in April 2017, the BlackBerry Keyone is a productivity-focused smartphone featuring a physical QWERTY keyboard and a 4.5-inch IPS LCD display (1080x1620). It is powered by a Snapdragon 625 chipset with options for 3GB or 4GB of RAM and 32GB or 64GB of storage. Key hardware includes a 12MP main camera capable of 4K video, an 8MP selfie camera, and a 3500 mAh battery with 18W fast charging. It runs Android 7.1 (upgradable to 8.1) and includes a front-mounted fingerprint sensor.

Released in June 2021, the Gionee Smartwatch 7 is a budget-friendly wearable (approx. 50 EUR) featuring a 1.3-inch TFT LCD display and an IP67 rating. It offers health tracking via accelerometer, heart rate, and SpO2 sensors, powered by a 130 mAh battery and Bluetooth 4.0, though it lacks cellular connectivity, Wi-Fi, and a camera.

Released in March 2021, the Coolpad Cool 10A is an entry-level Android 11 smartphone priced at approximately 90 EUR. It features a 6.52-inch IPS LCD display (720x1600), a Unisoc SC9863A octa-core chipset, 2GB of RAM, and 64GB of internal storage. The device is equipped with a 13MP dual rear camera, a 5MP selfie camera, and a 4000mAh battery with 10W wired charging.

Released in December 2022, the Wiko 5G is a HarmonyOS smartphone featuring a 6.78-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display and a Snapdragon 695 5G chipset. It is equipped with 8GB of RAM and storage options of 128GB or 256GB. Notable hardware includes a high-resolution 108MP quad-camera system, a 16MP selfie camera, and a 4000mAh battery supporting fast 66W wired charging. It is splash-resistant and priced at approximately 270 EUR.

The Philips I908 is a discontinued Dual SIM smartphone released in August 2015. It features a 5.0-inch Full HD IPS LCD display, an octa-core 1.7 GHz processor, 2GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage running Android 4.4.2. It is equipped with a 13MP main camera capable of 1080p video, a 5MP selfie camera, and a 3000 mAh Li-Ion battery.

The HP Elite x3 is a discontinued Windows 10 smartphone released in 2016. It features a 5.96-inch AMOLED display (1440x2560), a Snapdragon 820 processor, 4GB RAM, and 64GB of storage. Notable highlights include IP67 water resistance, MIL-STD-810G compliance, Bang & Olufsen stereo speakers, and Microsoft Continuum support. It is equipped with a 16MP main camera (4K video), an 8MP selfie camera, and a 4150 mAh battery with wireless charging.

Released in November 2023, the Infinix Smart 8 is an entry-level smartphone priced around 100 EUR. It features a 6.6-inch 90Hz IPS LCD display, 128GB storage with 8GB RAM, and is powered by a Unisoc T606 chipset on Android 13. The device includes a 13MP dual main camera, an 8MP selfie camera, and a large 5000mAh battery with 10W wired charging.

The BLU Studio X5 Max, released in July 2022, is an entry-level Android 11 (Go edition) smartphone priced around 50 EUR. It features a 5.7-inch IPS LCD display (480x960), a quad-core 1.3 GHz CPU, 2GB RAM, and 32GB of internal storage. The device is equipped with a 5MP dual main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and a removable 2700 mAh battery.

The Oukitel RT6 is a rugged 10.1-inch Android 13 tablet released in July 2023, designed for extreme durability with IP68/IP69K ratings, MIL-STD-810H compliance, and drop resistance. Its standout feature is a massive 20,000 mAh battery with 33W fast charging and reverse charging capabilities. Performance is driven by a Mediatek MT8788 chipset, 8GB RAM, and 256GB of UFS 2.1 storage. It features 16MP front and rear cameras, stereo speakers, and weighs 1030g, priced at approximately 350 EUR.

The LeEco Le 2 is a discontinued Android 6.0 smartphone released in April 2016. It features a 5.5-inch 1080p IPS LCD display, 3GB of RAM with 32GB or 64GB of internal storage, and is powered by either a Helio X20 or Snapdragon 652 chipset. Key hardware includes a 16MP main camera capable of 4K video, an 8MP selfie camera, and a 3000mAh battery with 18W fast charging. Notable additions include an infrared port and a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor, though it lacks a 3.5mm headphone jack and expandable memory.

The Kyocera Hydro Life is a discontinued, rugged Android 4.3 smartphone released in August 2014. It is highly durable, featuring IP57 dust/water resistance and MIL-STD-810G compliance. The device has a 4.5-inch IPS LCD (540 x 960), is powered by a Snapdragon 200 quad-core processor with 1.5GB RAM and 8GB internal storage, and includes a 5MP main camera and a 2000 mAh removable battery.

The Icemobile Prime 5.5 is a discontinued dual-SIM Android 4.4.2 (KitKat) smartphone released in August 2014. It features a 5.46-inch IPS LCD display (720x1280), a quad-core 1.3 GHz processor, 1GB of RAM, and 16GB of internal storage. The device is equipped with an 8MP main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and a removable 2250 mAh battery.

Released in September 2023, the Blackview A96 is an affordable smartphone ($161.69) featuring a 6.5-inch 120Hz IPS LCD display and a Mediatek Helio G99 chipset. It offers generous storage with 256GB internal memory and options for 8GB or 12GB of RAM. The device is equipped with a 48MP dual main camera, a 16MP selfie camera, and a 4380 mAh battery with 18W wired charging. It runs Android 13 and includes NFC and a side-mounted fingerprint sensor.

Released in Q3 2021, the Energizer U680S is an affordable Android 11 smartphone (~120 EUR) featuring a massive 7000 mAh battery and a large 6.8-inch IPS LCD display. It is powered by a Unisoc SC9863A octa-core chipset with 2GB RAM and 32GB storage, and includes a triple rear camera setup led by a 13MP sensor.

The Ericsson A2628 is a discontinued GSM phone announced in 2001. It features a basic monochrome graphic display with 4-line resolution, a Mini-SIM slot, and lacks a camera, Bluetooth, or WLAN. Key features include WAP 1.1 browsing, three built-in games, and a removable NiMH battery providing up to 11 hours of talk time with a high-capacity version. It was available in four colors and weighs 140g.

Released in February 2023, the Lava Yuva 2 Pro is an affordable Android 12 smartphone featuring a 6.52-inch IPS LCD display and a Mediatek Helio G37 chipset. It comes with 64GB storage, 4GB RAM, and a large 5000 mAh battery with 10W charging. The device includes a triple rear camera setup led by a 13MP wide lens and a 5MP selfie camera.

Released in September 2021, the Meizu 18s Pro is a high-end 5G smartphone featuring a 6.7-inch 120Hz Super AMOLED display with a QHD+ resolution. It is powered by the Snapdragon 888+ 5G chipset, paired with up to 12GB of RAM and 256GB of UFS 3.1 storage. The device boasts a triple main camera system led by a 50MP wide sensor with OIS, a 3x telephoto lens, and a 32MP ultrawide lens, complemented by a 44MP selfie camera. It is powered by a 4500 mAh battery supporting 40W wired and wireless charging, and includes an ultrasonic under-display fingerprint sensor.

The Spice Smart Flo 508 (Mi-508) is a discontinued budget Android 4.4.2 smartphone released in August 2014. It features a 5.0-inch IPS LCD display (480x854), a dual-core 1.3 GHz CPU, and minimal memory with 512MB RAM and 4GB internal storage. The device includes an 8MP main camera, a 2MP selfie camera, and is powered by a 2000 mAh Li-Ion battery.

The VK Mobile VK300 is a discontinued GSM mobile phone released in July 2005. This compact, lightweight device (75g) features a 1.8-inch TFT display and a secondary external screen, but lacks a camera, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and expandable memory. It is powered by a removable 720 mAh Li-Ion battery providing up to 3 hours of talk time.
